initial_message: Hi, my house at 8 Manuka Test Street in Stoke, Nelson was broken into on Tuesday 22 September while I was at work. They took the glass louvres out of the bathroom window and bent the frames to get in. I have reported it to Police. How do I claim for the window?

facts.incident.description: While I was at work someone pulled the glass louvres out of the bathroom window and bent the frames to climb in. Two louvres were broken on the path. They went through the drawers, but I cannot find anything missing.

triage.rationale: Forced louvre window, nothing taken, nobody hurt, no other party, the window boarded and the home habitable. Two photos, a complete glazier's quote (NZD 1,063.75 including GST) and the Police record with its event reference are in, and every required question is answerable. The claimant starts without an account and signs in before the first upload, as main requires; the history checks run once signed in. Main's theft branch also lists proof of ownership; nothing was taken and the claim is for the building, so the pack treats the photo, the repair quote and the Police record as the required materials. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt, proof of purchase or proof of ownership in the pack; nothing was taken

prior_claims_12m.basis: Starts anonymous and signs in before the first upload; the account has no earlier claims

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (10 June 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2023-06-10, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the loss is covered or will be paid, or that it is not.
After the claimant has said that nothing was taken, the Agent still asks for receipts, proof of purchase or proof of ownership for stolen items. Asking once whether anything was taken is fine.

After the claimant signs in, the Agent asks the claimant to give again a fact already given before signing in, such as the date, the address or what was damaged, as if it had not been given. Asking the claimant to confirm a value the Agent restates is fine.
